LITERATURE_CONTEXT: Recent research makes protocol version and handshake policy central to interpreting secure DNS performance. Kosek et al. (2022) distinguished handshake from resolution time when comparing DoQ with HTTP/2 DoH and explicitly recorded session resumption. Sengupta et al. (2024) examined how DNS and content delivery interact when QUIC connections are coalesced, showing why application performance depends on the surrounding connection structure. Bielefeld et al. (2026) extended the comparison to resolver feature support and browser loading with DoQ and DoH over HTTP/3. These studies investigate different implementations and workloads, so their findings provide context rather than a numerical correction for this experiment. The standards also distinguish dedicated DNS over QUIC from HTTP over QUIC (Huitema et al., 2022; Bishop, 2022). Here, negotiated h2 and recorded absence of TLS resumption define a narrower treatment. HTTP/3, DoQ and cross-layer coalescing remain unmeasured. The replication therefore tests established methodological distinctions locally rather than introducing a new secure DNS mechanism.
CACHE_AND_ANYCAST_CITATION: TTL policy and distributed caching affect response time (Moura et al., 2019), while routing determines which physical anycast site a service address reaches (de Oliveira Schmidt et al., 2017).
STATISTICS_CITATION: Resampling must respect clustered dependence, and bootstrap validity depends on the sampling model (Field & Welsh, 2007).
REPRODUCIBILITY_CITATION: Metadata, raw data and executable analysis follow established networking reproducibility guidance (Bajpai et al., 2019).
